items.headline: Apps you connect to Claude can now bring their own 'how-to' know-how, and run long jobs in the background
items.summary: Anthropic says services you plug into Claude through MCP (the standard way outside apps connect to Claude) can now ship 'skills', step-by-step instructions Claude loads only when a task needs them. It's a public beta, on by default for Pro, Max and Ultra plans. Connected apps can also run slow jobs in the background and pause to ask you before anything paid or destructive.
items.why_it_matters: If you connect Claude to tools like Shopify or HubSpot, Claude should now follow those companies' own best-practice steps instead of guessing, and it will check with you before it spends money or deletes something.

items.headline: New York bans AI chatbot toys for five years, but not until after the holidays
items.summary: Gov. Kathy Hochul signed a law banning the making and selling of toys with built-in AI chatbots, like talking stuffed animals and robots, after watchdog tests found some had inappropriate conversations with kids. It kicks in 90 days after signing, around late February, so these toys can still be sold this holiday season. New York is the second state after California to do this.
items.why_it_matters: If you're shopping for kids or grandkids this season, think twice about 'AI-powered' talking toys, and if you sell products with AI baked in, states are clearly willing to step in when kids are involved.

items.headline: Whatnot drops its seller fee to 0% for Black Friday as live shopping gets crowded
items.summary: The live-selling app Whatnot is charging sellers no commission on Black Friday (and on Saturday for eligible small sellers), then half off through Cyber Monday, with giveaway streams from big names like MrBeast and Kai Cenat running Nov 27 to 30. eBay is offering 0% on its own live sales too, as both chase TikTok Shop.
items.why_it_matters: Selling on a livestream is becoming a real option for small businesses with physical products, and platforms are now cutting fees to win sellers, so it's a cheap weekend to see if live selling fits your business.
